prompt: A city's bus ridership fell 15% in two years while the population grew 3%. Average trip times rose 20%. Which is the strongest initial hypothesis?

options.text: People have probably soured on the buses.
options.feedback: Too vague to test: soured why, and what data would show it?

options.text: Slower trips are likely pushing riders to drive instead.
options.feedback: Right. Trip times rose 20% as ridership fell. I'd compare ridership changes on routes where trip times rose most and least.

options.text: A shrinking population is likely cutting the number of riders.
Riders are likely paying more in fares than they can afford.
options.feedback: Nothing mentions fares, and it ignores the 20% rise in trip times.

explanation: The data shows ridership down 15% as trip times rose 20%, while the population grew. Likely cause: slower trips are pushing riders to drive. To test it, compare ridership changes on routes that slowed most and least. If they fell alike, look at fares or service frequency.
